x_posts.label: Post 3

research.facts:
Munetaka Murakami HR Record
**Sources:**
- Yahoo Sports — "Munetaka Murakami hits 7th HR in 21st MLB game, breaks Ohtani's Japanese-born record" (HIGH)
- CBS Sports — Murakami 7 HRs in first 21 games confirmed, surpassing Ohtani's 5 (HIGH)
- Chicago Sun-Times — Murakami debut, early HR pace coverage (HIGH)
- MLB.com — Player page + IL placement (Grade 2 right hamstring strain) (HIGH)
- Bleacher Report — Murakami season overview (MEDIUM)
**Key Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- Munetaka Murakami debuted March 26, 2026 (Opening Day) — homered in his first MLB at-bat
- Hit 7 home runs in his first 21 MLB games — most by any Japanese-born player in their first 21 MLB games
- This surpasses Shohei Ohtani's 5 HRs in first 21 games (2018) — the previous Japanese-born player record
- His season continued: 10 HRs in first 25 games; 20 HRs in first 55 games (third all-time, behind Bellinger 22 in 2017 and Berger 21 in 1930)
- Murakami is a two-time NPB Triple Crown winner — Japan's premier power hitter
- He suffered a Grade 2 right hamstring strain and was placed on the IL, missing approximately 35 games
- Was nearing a rehab assignment with Triple-A Charlotte in early July
- His August 11 active-roster status is unconfirmed (on IL or nearing return — check MLB.com transactions)
**Distinction from separate record:**
- Toronto Blue Jays' Kazuma Okamoto separately broke Ohtani's record for most home runs by a Japanese-born player in a full ROOKIE SEASON — a different record; do not conflate
**Freshness:** Milestone occurred earlier in the 2026 season (first 21 games, approx. April); revisiting as Murakami approaches return from IL. Historical record stands regardless of injury.
